items: Track Your Daily App Usage: Use your phone's screen-time settings or download a tracking app to measure exactly how many hours you spend on dating apps each week.
Complete the 7-Day App Usage Log: Record the time of day, duration, emotional state before opening, and emotional state after closing every time you use any dating app for seven consecutive days.
Record Emotional States Before and After: Note your feelings each time you open a dating app so you can identify which emotions—boredom, loneliness, anxiety—trigger your scroll behavior.
Identify Your Top Three Scroll Triggers: Write down the three specific moments when you most often open apps without consciously deciding to, such as evening boredom or post-date disappointment.
Choose Two Non-Negotiable App-Free Windows: Pick specific time blocks, such as before 10am and after 9pm, where you commit to never opening any dating app regardless of willpower.
Delete All Dating Apps From Your Phone Entirely: Remove the apps completely rather than just logging out, because re-downloading them later creates the friction you need to break the habit loop.
Set a Five-Minute Timer When You Open Any App: Open your phone's timer the moment you start browsing and close the app immediately when it rings, regardless of where you are in a conversation.
Tell Someone About Your Boundaries or Set Phone Reminders: Share your app-free windows with a friend or set calendar alerts so your commitments stay visible and harder to ignore.
Replace Evening App Use With a Specific Alternative Activity: When boredom hits at night, have a ready替代 such as reading, journaling, or calling a friend instead of defaulting to scrolling.
Create a Post-Date Rule to Wait Before Opening Apps: Prevent quick rebound browsing after disappointing dates by imposing a 24-hour app-free period following any date.
Schedule Social Activities During High-Risk Times: Plan in-person gatherings, classes, or hobbies during weekends and holidays when loneliness spikes make you most vulnerable to excessive app use.

Turn Procrastination Triggers Into Action Signals: When you catch yourself reaching for the app to avoid something difficult, pause and do the harder task instead—this builds the discipline apps erode.
